readouts.finding:
LINE 2: DON'T PLOW
FOR THE HARVEST.
readouts.why: Line 2 (不耕穫) in the Cheng Yi / Zhu Xi reading is working without counting on the crop, which is 'do what's right, not what pays' almost word for word. Caveat: the input's literal English ('not plowing yet reaping') and Wang Bi ('completes what another began, does not claim the merit') read it differently, so the finding leans on the later reading; the safer but flatter option is line 1, 'AT THE BASE: GO OUT\nWITHOUT FALSENESS.' (fit 6).
readouts.lineText: Not plowing yet reaping, not clearing new fields yet having mature land—then it is beneficial to have a place to go.

readouts.finding:
LINE 3: DRILL THE CHARIOT
DAILY. THEN SET OUT.
readouts.why: Line 3 says 'practice guarding the chariot (daily)... benefit in having a destination': practise first, then go, which is the lesson 'store up strength, then use it' and answers the hook about years of practice. Line 6 ('how vast the thoroughfare of Heaven') is the payoff image but says only the second half.
readouts.lineText: Fine horses give chase. Benefit in difficult Correctness. It is said: practice guarding the chariot. Benefit in having a destination.

readouts.why: The lesson 'be moved as you move others' is about the whole shape, every line answered by its partner; no single line says it. The lines climb the body (toe, calf, thigh, back, jaw) and mostly warn against restless or shallow influence. Option only: line 6, 'AT THE TOP: ONLY JAW,\nCHEEKS AND TONGUE.', would carry a different lesson such as 'Talk alone moves no one.' Data note: lines 3 and 6 in the input hold the Image text, not the line statement.

readouts.finding:
AT THE BASE: THE TAIL
OF THE RETREAT. DANGER.
readouts.why: Line 1 (遯尾，厲) is the last one out, caught by the danger: the plain warning behind 'go while you still can go freely'. Wang Bi: 'when danger has arrived and only then does one seek to move, it is difficult to avoid peril.' Alternative: line 6 'Bountiful retreat. Nothing that is not beneficial' (leaving early and free). Data note: the input's line 1 holds Wang Bi's note, not the statement 遯尾，厲，勿用有攸往 ('Retreating at the tail. Danger. Do not set out.').
readouts.lineText: Retreating at the tail. Danger. Do not set out.

readouts.finding:
LINE 3: THE RAM BUTTS
THE FENCE. HORNS CAUGHT.
readouts.why: Line 3 sets 'the petty person uses vigor; the noble person does not' beside the ram that butts a fence and gets its horns stuck: strength used wrongly traps itself, the reverse side of 'be strong only in what is right'. Line 4 (the fence breaks open) could follow, but one line is enough.
readouts.lineText: The petty person uses vigor; the noble person uses restraint. Correctness brings danger. A ram butts against a fence and entangles its horns.

readouts.finding:
AT THE TOP: ADVANCING
WITH THE HORNS.
readouts.why: Line 6 (晉其角) is advance by force, horns first, even attacking a town; Wang Bi: 'already at the horn yet still pressing forward, how is this not excessive?' It carries the 'don't push' half clearly; the 'shine' half is left to the lesson line. Alternative: line 4, 'advancing like a hamster' (grasping advance).
readouts.lineText: Advancing to the horn. One resorts to attacking the city. Danger, then good fortune, and no blame. Yet correctness brings regret.

readouts.why: 'Home in order, the rest follows' is about everyone in their place, which the whole-shape finding shows; no one line says it. Line 1 ('setting barriers for the household') is literally rules, which contradicts the meaning card 'skip the rules'. Option only: line 6, 'AT THE TOP: SINCERE\nAND DIGNIFIED.' ('there is sincerity and a dignified bearing, in the end good fortune'), fits the meaning card 'Say real things' and a lesson like 'Be sincere, not strict.' The current finding uses the ANSWER jargon.
readouts.loopNote: Meaning 'skip the rules' sits awkwardly with the hexagram's line 1 and line 3, which favour strictness; the hook-to-lesson loop itself holds.

readouts.finding:
LINE 2: MEETS HIS LORD
IN A SIDE STREET.
readouts.why: Line 2 (遇主于巷): both partners are out of place, yet they still find each other by a back way; Wang Bi: 'both seek their kindred... meet'. That is 'apart, but still answering' and fits 'start small'. Option: line 6 (draws the bow, then lays it down: 'not a bandit but a marriage partner') is the stronger image but carries a different lesson, that the one you oppose may be a partner.
readouts.lineText: One meets the master in an alleyway. No blame.

readouts.why: Line 5 (大蹇，朋來) says the hook, meaning card and question ('ask for help', 'who could you ask?') directly, but not the current lesson. For 'look at yourself' the best line is line 1 ('going forth meets obstruction; turning back brings praise'), fit 5 at most; the lesson comes from the hexagram image (反身修德), not a line. Option: lesson 'Blocked? Ask for help.' Data note: the input's line 6 holds the Image text.
readouts.loopNote: The loop breaks at the lesson: hook, meaning and question are about asking for help, then the lesson turns to self-examination. Line 5 with a lesson like 'Blocked? Ask for help.' closes the loop.

readouts.finding:
LINE 5: THE NOBLE ONE
UNTIES THE KNOT.
readouts.why: No line says 'don't linger'; that comes from the Judgment (有攸往，夙吉, 'if there is somewhere to go, early is good'). Line 5 (君子維有解... 有孚于小人) is the noble person releasing, with trust shown even to petty people, which fits the meaning card 'let the grudges go' and the question 'what can you forgive?'. Option: lesson 'Out of danger? Let the grudges go.' Fit against the current lesson: 4. Alternative image: line 4, 'release your big toe; then allies come'.
readouts.lineText: The noble person herein achieves release—good fortune. There is trust shown toward the petty person.
readouts.loopNote: Hook to lesson ('pressure's off?' to 'don't linger') holds, but meaning and question (forgive, grudges) point elsewhere; line 5 would tie the finding to them.

readouts.finding:
LINE 4: CUT WHAT AILS YOU.
SOON THERE IS JOY.
readouts.why: The lesson 'two small baskets are enough' is from the Judgment (二簋可用享); no line carries it. Line 4 (損其疾，使遄有喜) fits the meaning card 'cut the anger, cut the wants' and the question 'what can you let go of?'. Option: lesson 'Cut what hurts you. Do it soon.' Line 3 ('three travel, one is lost; one alone finds a friend') is the other candidate but harder for a newcomer.
readouts.lineText: Decrease one's affliction. Act swiftly and there will be joy. No blame.
